text:
carla (acme): Hey team — we rotated our API key via the customer portal ~10:03 UTC and since ~10:05 all our requests to /v1/generate are returning 401. We rolled back the key but still seeing 401s intermittently. Can someone help?

maya (support): sorry you're hitting this — can you paste a failing curl and the header you're using? also which region are you hitting?

carla (acme): curl -s -D - -o /dev/null -H "Authorization: ApiKey sk-prod-xxxxnew" https://api.redwood.cloud/v1/generate
returns: HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
www-authenticate: ApiKey realm="redwood"

carla (acme): region is us-west-2, clients in eu-west seem fine for some of our users.

maya (support): pinging infra + security. @alex @priya — sounds like key revocation/propagation; we rotated from the portal which should write to Vault -> publish revocation event -> edge cache invalidation.

alex (infra): looking at the revocation queue now. I see the new key version for tenant acme-42 rolled into Vault at 10:03:21, but the revocation publish to ns://revocations failed for shard-3 with a 409: "node id mismatch". So the publish didn't reach edge consumers in us-west-2.

priya (security): curious — if publish failed, should that cause 401s or 200s? I'd expect old key still accepted until edges pick up revocation. explain repro: some nodes rejecting, some accepting?

alex (infra): right — the current system is: new key stored in Vault (versioned), revocation record written to revocations DB, then we publish a delta to NATS. Edge nodes subscribe and flush caches for the tenant. In this case revocations DB entry exists, but the NATS publish failed for one shard, so half the edge fleet kept accepting the rotated (old) key and half were seeing the new-permitted-but-old-revoked mismatch, causing intermittent 401s.

maya (support): tl;dr: race + failed publish led to inconsistent auth state across edges.

carla (acme): Ugh. How do we get everything back to working state?

alex (infra): immediate mitigation: force a full revocation broadcast and then trigger an edge cache flush for acme-42 in us-west-2. Running admin command now.

deploy-bot: [deploy] started full-revocation-broadcast job id=rb-20260710-0310 by alex

alex (infra): running: 
```
POST https://internal.redwood.svc/admin/v1/tenants/acme-42/flush-revocations
Body: {"force": true}
```

alex (infra): Also flushing redis edge caches: 
```
redis-cli -h redis-edge-usw2 KEYS "tenant:acme-42:*" | xargs -n100 redis-cli -h redis-edge-usw2 DEL
```

tom (sre): i'll watch the error rate on /v1/generate for acme-42. setting alert: support-acme-401s if 401 rate > 5% for 2min.

priya (security): follow-up: we should confirm the KMS wrapping version used for the stored key — if the portal rotated but the client is still signing with old wrapped key, that'd also cause rejects. alex can you verify KMS key id/vv?

alex (infra): confirmed: Vault shows secret.version=2 for acme-42 and wraps with kms-key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111:key/abcd. Last KMS rotate was 30d ago; no mismatch there. The failure path looks specifically like missing publish to NATS.

maya (support): carla — we triggered the forced broadcast and cache flush. can you try your curl again?

carla (acme): retesting now...

carla (acme): good news: curl now returns 200. Thanks. Looks stable for the last 30s.

alex (infra): logs show publish retry succeeded and edge subscribers picked up the revocation at 10:06:12. The earlier 409 happened because the publisher attempted to publish from a stale leader instance; we have a race bug in leader election + publisher assignment.

priya (security): we'll create a mitigation: if DB revocation exists but publish fails, schedule immediate retry and mark shard unhealthy. Also add metrics for publish failure counts by shard.

maya (support): notes for the customer: 1) if rotating keys, wait for propagation (we'll add clearer guidance) 2) if you see 401s after rotate, tell us immediate region + sample curl and we'll force a broadcast 

alex (infra): internal TODOs: create ticket INF-3245 to add retry-on-fail logic + alert when publishing 5x fails in 10m; add small playbook for support to force broadcast without dev infra intervention.

priya (security): security follow-up: audit the portal flow to ensure publish is synchronous-fail-fast or has at-least-once guarantee. If not, document eventual-consistency window.

carla (acme): appreciate the fast turnaround. can you send a short summary we can attach to our internal incident log?

maya (support): sure — I'll paste a short incident summary in here in 10m and follow up with the ticket numbers. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: [deploy] finished job rb-20260710-0310 status=success duration=22s

maya (support): INCIDENT SUMMARY DRAFT — feel free to copy: 
- timeline: 10:03:21 rotated API key via portal -> 10:04:00 revocations DB entry created -> 10:04:05 NATS publish failed for shard-3 (409 node-id mismatch) -> 10:06:12 forced broadcast + cache flush -> 10:06:30 customer reports success.
- root cause: publisher assignment race caused missed publish for a subset of edge subscribers leading to inconsistent auth state and intermittent 401s.
- mitigations: forced broadcast + edge redis flush to recover immediately; INF-3245 to add retry/alerts; update portal to ensure publish at-least-once semantics.
- customer impact: acme-42 experienced ~3 minutes of intermittent 401s in us-west-2 only.

carla (acme): perfect. thanks everyone. will close on our side after we validate for an hour.

maya (support): thanks — leave the thread open until you confirm. I'll ping when INF-3245 is created.

tom (sre): keeping watch for 10 more mins. setting a bookmark.
